description: Finsupp.single_eval_le_sum bounds a coefficient without splitting support membership, including zero coefficients outside the support.
Expanding with hasseDeriv_apply before applying the norm bound avoids tracking the image of derivative support.
Finset.le_prod_of_submultiplicative_of_nonneg lifts a nonnegative submultiplicative function to finite products, replacing manual insertion induction.
List.ofFn_injective and cancellation of precomposition by a surjective equivalence transport a base-digit sum equality directly to Finsupp equality, removing a bespoke uniqueness wrapper.

Restricting a polynomial submodule to the coefficient field allows Submodule.smul_mem_iff to cancel a nonzero natural scalar in the Hasse-derivative recurrence, avoiding an explicit reciprocal-polynomial identity.
Finset.sum_fn normalizes sums of row functions before application; together with Pi.smul_def it avoids a separate matrix-extensionality equality when using multilinear finite-sum expansion.

AlgHom.map_det with Matrix.map normalization lets terminal simpa transport a finite row determinant expansion through Kronecker substitution, removing a RingHom coercion round-trip and summand congruence.

List.forall_mem_ofFn_iff proves digit bounds directly, avoiding broad simp attempts to synthesize Nonempty for a possibly empty Fin type. Combining it with exact list-index rewrites reduced kroneckerExp_injOn from 1311.73 to 164.75 ms and 6773 to 643 heartbeats.

Unsqueezing a simpa used to infer a sum_le_sum bound simplified r + 1 - 1 - j to r - j, preventing sum_range_reflect matching. A restricted simp set is required while the intermediate reflected index is inferred.
simp [Finsupp.mapDomain_of_notMem_range] discharges Fin.last outside the range of Fin.castSucc and the singleton evaluation, eliminating an explicit non-range contradiction.

Elementary sqrt bounds require Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt, and Fin.prod_univ_castSucc requires Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin. These defining imports compile the full lattice estimate without importing complex powers or square-root smoothness.

Count bounded polynomial families by transporting bounded whole coefficient arrays through AddMonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff. Finset.card_finsupp and Finsupp.card_Iic support arbitrary variable types with finitely supported degree bounds; finprod_eq_prod_of_fintype recovers the original finite-index formula. Actual final source, old-contract recovery and TYPE/VALUE/standard-axiom guards passed.

For x>0 and c>=1, Real.add_rpow_le_rpow_add gives x^c+1 <= (x+1)^c. Nat.floor_le and (x^c)^2>0 then yield 2*floor(x^c)+1 < (x+1)^(2*c). This supports positive real bases and the c=1 endpoint in the strict counting bound; actual old-contract recovery, boundary cases and TYPE/opaque VALUE/standard-axiom checks passed.

For simultaneous monic polynomial remainders, encode only coefficients below natDegree as a bounded finite function. Fintype.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt supplies a common distinct pair, and Polynomial.sum_modByMonic_coeff reconstructs all remainders at once. Explicit cardinality simp rules avoid expensive broad subtype/interval simplification. Actual original-contract recovery, common-witness properties and TYPE/opaque VALUE/standard-axiom guards passed.

For integer coefficients in [0,B], abs_sub_le_of_nonneg_of_le bounds their difference directly; one Int.cast_abs rewrite and exact_mod_cast avoid repeated real casts. The additive lemma is generated by to_additive on mabs_div_le_of_one_le_of_le. This permits arbitrary variable types without finite-support assumptions; actual old-contract recovery, seven full-premise counters and closed TYPE/opaque VALUE/standard-axiom gates passed.

Equal polynomial remainders yield divisibility via dvd_modByMonic_iff_dvd without monicity; evaluation at a root then vanishes. comp_aeval_apply transports diagonal multivariate evaluation directly, allowing arbitrary variable types and commutative target rings without changing the existing integer-coefficient diag API or adding a helper. Actual old finite-real contract/wholeproof recovery, nonmonic/nilpotent/trivial-ring properties and closed TYPE/opaque VALUE/standard-axiom gates passed.

A weighted-index lower bound needs vanishing only strictly below the cutoff. Nonzero derivatives force their coordinate degrees into the bounding box, so the unrestricted le_index_iff characterization gives a direct contradiction proof. Expressing box membership as coordinate inequalities avoids a DecidableEq instance while mem_box.2 recovers finite-box callers. Actual exact old contracts/wholeproof closures, sharp positive-cutoff and zero-bound counters, closed TYPE/opaque VALUE/std3 and matched target profiles passed.

Scale a division inequality by the positive square of a denominator inferred nonzero from the positive quadratic bound. This avoids denominator sign cases and turns the key step into a strict contraction δ*m<1. Actual ordered-semifield/NNReal applications, exact original logarithmic contract recovery, boundary counters and closed TYPE/opaque VALUE/std3 gates passed. Explicit scalar type and direct cutoff/product certificates reduce delayed-inference caller cost; paired residual overhead is still disclosed.

When applying a minimum-image bound to a weighted error function on integer/natural pairs, supply the known pair explicitly: an underscore caused costly expected-type unification through the unfolded function. Actual same-source final and repeat failed at 2289.463/2314.001 ms; the repaired exact-prefix target passed at 291.597 ms with unchanged statement and default proof checks, without a controlled ratio claim across runtime contexts.

before_code:
variable {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]

omit [DecidableEq σ] in
theorem Θ_nonneg ...
description: Independent review found 35 `omit [DecidableEq σ] in` lines cancelling instance variables no declaration used (degreeOf no longer needs DecidableEq). If every declaration mentioning a variable has to `omit` its instance, drop the instance from the `variable` line instead; `#check @decl` shows which instances a def actually takes.

before_code:
variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
noncomputable def wronskian (φ : Fin l → K[X]) : K[X] := ...
after_code:
variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
noncomputable def wronskian (φ : Fin l → R[X]) : R[X] := ...
description: Definitions and structural lemmas stated over `Field K` (wronskianMatrix, wronskian, kronecker, coeff_kronecker, diag, geom_sum_le_one_add_pow, degreeOf_det_hasseDeriv_le) compiled verbatim at CommRing/CommSemiring; only the lemmas using `Fintype.linearIndependent_iff` (Ring), division by `μ + 1` (Field) or `Nat.cast_choose_eq_descPochhammer_div` (CharZero field) needed the stronger class. Split the variable block into CommSemiring/CommRing/Field sections rather than one `[Field K]` for the whole file. A generic ring needs `rw [← map_intCast C]` before `degreeOf_C_mul_le` where the ℤ version got it by defeq.

have := congrArg (map f) h0
rw [genWronskian, RingHom.map_det, map_zero] at this
rw [genWronskian, ← this]
congr 1

simp [hasseDeriv_map]
after_code: exact ⟨D, hD, fun h0 ↦ hne (by rw [← map_genWronskian, h0, map_zero])⟩
description: The same 5-line skeleton (`genWronskian, (Alg|Ring)Hom.map_det, congr 1, ext, simp [hasseDeriv_*]`) appeared three times across two files and `degreeOf i (rename f p) = 0` for `i ∉ range f` was re-proved inline four times by unfolding `degreeOf`. A reviewer unanchored on the proofs spots these; extract `map_genWronskian`, `rename_genWronskian`, `degreeOf_rename_of_notMem_range` and the call sites collapse to one line each.

Removing `import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.CommRing` from HasseDeriv.lean (unused there, verified by compiling the file alone) broke CoeffNorm.lean, which used `MvPolynomial.support_neg` through the transitive import. When deleting imports from a root module, rebuild the whole library and move the import to the file that actually uses the lemma.

before_code:
have hc : ContinuousAt (fun δ ↦ (m : ℝ) * (1 + 4 * δ) / (gam δ n m - eta δ m)) 0 :=
  (show ContinuousAt ... from continuousAt_const.mul (...)).div (...) (...).ne'
after_code:
have hc : ContinuousAt (fun δ ↦ (m : ℝ) * (1 + 4 * δ) / (gam δ n m - eta δ m)) 0 := by
  unfold gam eta
  fun_prop (disch := first | positivity | assumption)
description: Ten-line hand-assembled `continuousAt_const.mul (...)` chains close with `unfold gam eta; fun_prop (disch := first | positivity | assumption)` once the project-local defs are unfolded (`fun_prop` reports 'No theorems found for Roth.gam' otherwise). Likewise `P %ₘ f = Q %ₘ f` proved by unfolding `modByMonic` to `divModByMonicAux` is replaced by the stable API `div_modByMonic_unique` + `modByMonic_add_div` + `degree_modByMonic_lt` at the same length.

before_code:
(ih : ∀ {δ : ℝ}, 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1) → ∀ {r q}, … )
… (ih hε0 (mul_one_add_one_div_lt_aux n hδ).le)
description: A premise `δ ≤ 1/(n+1)` threaded through the private helpers of an induction was dead: the real `ih` produced by `induction n generalizing δ` never had it (hover on `ih` shows the type), and the main theorem discarded it with `fun {δ} hδ0 _ ↦ ih hδ0`. A whole helper lemma existed only to discharge it. When auxiliary lemmas take an `ih` argument, copy its type from the hover of the actual `ih`, not from the paper's hypotheses.

before_code: Polynomial.aeval (X none : MvPolynomial (Option τ) R) V
description: Mathlib's name for the embedding `R[X] → MvPolynomial σ R` sending `X` to `X i` is `Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i` (with `_C`, `_X`, `_injective`, `_eq_rename_comp`, `eval_/aeval_/rename_toMvPolynomial`); spelling it `Polynomial.aeval (X i)` hides this API. The def is `aeval (X i)` by `rfl`, so proofs that used `aeval` lemmas need `Polynomial.toMvPolynomial` unfolded once (`rw`/`simp only`). One `change` that abstracted a subterm under the bundled hom hit a heartbeat timeout; abstracting with `obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, ∀ ν ρ, … = a ν ρ := ⟨_, fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩` and `simp_rw [ha]` avoided the defeq check.

Counting a box of `Fin (n+1) →₀ ℕ` fibrewise: mathlib has `Finsupp.cons`/`Finsupp.tail` with `cons_zero`, `cons_succ`, `tail_cons`, `cons_tail` for the FIRST coordinate (no `snoc`). Fibring over coordinate 0 with `Finset.card_bij' (fun d _ ↦ Finsupp.cons i d) (fun d _ ↦ Finsupp.tail d)` replaced a hand-rolled `mapDomain Fin.castSucc + single (Fin.last m) i` plus two evaluation lemmas and a 25-line `card_bij`. `simpa` needs `Finsupp.tail_apply` passed explicitly (not simp).

before_code:
rw [degreeOf_eq_sup, support_map_of_injective _ Int.cast_injective, ← degreeOf_eq_sup]
exact hQd j
description: Three review rounds kept finding the same two categories the author missed: (i) a fact re-derived inline at 3–4 sites in different spellings (`degreeOf j (map f P) ≤ r j` via `degreeOf`/`degrees_map_of_injective` at some sites and `degreeOf_eq_sup`/`support_map_of_injective` at others) — extract it (`degreeOf_map_of_injective`, absent from mathlib); (ii) dead `classical` lines (34 removed over three rounds; the ones actually needed are those feeding `DecidableEq`-dependent lemmas like `coeff_monomial`, `Finset.biUnion`, `box`). Checking each `classical` by deleting it is cheap and should be part of cleanup.

Naming hypotheses after paper equation numbers (`h32`, `h33`, `h47'`) in public signatures is flagged by a fresh reviewer because named arguments then require the PDF; keep the equation number in the docstring and name the hypothesis by content (`hratio`, `hlogq`, `hqr`). Likewise a def that is unfolded at every use (`wronskianMatrix`, `mainCoeffBound`) or that duplicates a mathlib object (`kroneckerExp` = `Finsupp.weight …`) is better inlined or made an `abbrev` of the mathlib def with an `_apply` lemma.
